w: These fault-block mountains hide the oldest rock in Texas: Precambrian stone 1.25 billion years old, exposed by crustal rifting along the Rio Grande over the last 10 million years. The range's spine climbs to 7,192 feet at North Franklin Peak, running 23 miles from central El Paso north into New Mexico.
s: Texas's oldest rock, 1.25 billion years old
_facts: Contains 1.25-billion-year-old Precambrian rock, oldest in Texas
North Franklin Peak reaches 7,192 feet
23 miles long, formed by Rio Grande rift extension
Runs from El Paso into New Mexico

w: First lit as a Christmas decoration in 1940, this 459-bulb star on the Franklin Mountains was meant to signal peace across the nearby US-Mexico border during the holidays. Visible from the air up to 100 miles away and once compared to Virginia's Roanoke Star, it's now kept lit year-round by the El Paso Chamber.
s: A wartime peace signal, now lit year-round
_facts: First lit as a Christmas decoration in 1940
459 bulbs, visible from up to 100 miles in the air
Meant as a peace signal across the US-Mexico border
Now maintained and lit year-round

a: near the border, south El Paso
w: This National Park Service site commemorates the peaceful resolution of the Chamizal dispute, a decades-long argument over shifting Rio Grande banks that put a sliver of land in contention between the US and Mexico. Sitting right on the international boundary, it turns a diplomatic settlement into a walkable place.
s: The park marking a border dispute's peaceful end
_facts: A National Park Service site
Commemorates the Chamizal boundary dispute settlement
Located directly on the US-Mexico border
Also listed as an NRHP district

w: Built in 1930, this downtown landmark still runs as it always has, its 2,050-seat Kendall Kidd Performance Hall and smaller 200-seat Philanthropy Theatre hosting Broadway tours, concerts, and solo acts. Every summer it anchors the Plaza Classic Film Festival, a National Historic Building still doing its original job.
s: A 1930 movie palace still running film and Broadway
_facts: Built in 1930
2,050-seat Kendall Kidd Performance Hall plus 200-seat Philanthropy Theatre
A National Historic Building of Significance
Hosts the annual Plaza Classic Film Festival

n: El Paso Holocaust Museum and Study Center
w: Holocaust survivor Henry Kellen founded this museum in 1994 to keep the history of Nazi concentration camps and wartime resistance movements in public memory. Run on donations and grants rather than a government budget, it remains a modest, survivor-built counterweight to forgetting.
s: A Holocaust museum founded by a survivor
_facts: Founded in 1994 by Holocaust survivor Henry Kellen
Located at 715 N. Oregon Street
Educates on Nazi camps and resistance movements
Funded through donations and grants

w: At 24,247 acres, this is one of the largest urban parks in the US to sit entirely within a city's limits, wrapping the Franklin Mountains around northern El Paso. Its headquarters sit at 5,426 feet elevation, with North Franklin Mountain topping out at 7,192 feet inside the park's own boundary.
s: One of America's largest parks, wholly inside a city
_facts: One of the largest urban parks in the US entirely within city limits
Headquarters at 5,426 feet elevation
Highest point, North Franklin Mountain, reaches 7,192 feet

w: Spanish conquistadors, Franciscan clerics, and Tigua Indians founded this settlement between October 9 and 12, 1680, fleeing the Pueblo Revolt in New Mexico along the Rio Grande's southern bank. It stands as the oldest European settlement in what is now Texas, predating the state itself by over a century.
_facts: Founded October 9-12, 1680
Settled by Spanish, Franciscans, and Tigua Indians fleeing the Pueblo Revolt
Oldest European settlement in present-day Texas
Located on the Rio Grande's southern bank

w: Named for Abraham Chavez, the El Paso Symphony's longtime conductor, this 2,500-seat concert hall went up in the early 1970s, its curved frame visible mid-construction in the background of Steve McQueen's 1972 film The Getaway. Its glass entrance and lobby still host the symphony and touring acts today.
s: A 1970s concert hall that cameoed in The Getaway
_facts: Named for conductor Abraham Chavez
Built in the early 1970s
Under-construction frame appears in the 1972 film The Getaway
2,500 seats, three-story glass entrance

w: Zack White built this 1912 hotel to be fireproof after watching another El Paso hotel burn, sending architect Henry Trost to study San Francisco's earthquake survivors first. Its Tiffany-style glass lobby dome once framed guests watching Mexican Revolution gunfights from the roof; six presidents have stayed since.
s: Where guests once watched revolution gunfights
_facts: Opened Thanksgiving Day 1912, designed by Trost & Trost
45-foot Tiffany-style stained glass lobby dome
Guests watched 1914 Mexican Revolution firefights from the roof
